newsitem.title: USA: Most IMM currency futures close thin trade higher.
newsitem.headline: Most IMM currency futures close thin trade higher.

text.p: IMM currency futures closed an afternoon of thin trading mostly higher but off session peaks.

Traders said futures moved upward much of the afternoon, poking up to session highs late and then eroding again in turnover dominated by dealer and bank bidding, with little outside participation evident.

"We hit airpockets," said one floor broker of the afternoon's rise, which he said triggered buystops in March Swiss francs near $0.7620, or about 1.3235 spot, and near $0.6500 in nearby marks, or roughly 1.5475 spot. "Then there was nothing on the downside."
Some tied the drift higher partly to erosion in U.S. stock and bond markets, where prices gave back small morning gains and gradually moved lower much of the afternoon.
After IMM currency futures closed Monday, stock index futures plummeted to large losses in suddenly busy trade.
Currency traders noted some edginess about Tuesday's Federal Open Market Committee meeting, although almost everyone looked for steady rate policy.
"No one's expecting anything (from FOMC). If they did anything, it would be to lower rates," said one floor broker. "I think everyone's just kind of standing back and watching."
Some Eurodollar traders have noted a back-month price bias suggesting steady to slightly easier policy in the next year.

The mark during the morning met continued selling from last week's announcement that European Union leaders had hammered out a proposed fiscal pact seen as containing some compromise on Germany's hard-line approach to the union.

The drop reported Monday in Germany's IFO economics institute business climate index for November added pressure on the mark, which still managed to keep gains against the technically and fundamentally weak Swiss franc.
Sterling popped up and expanded its gains.

The Organization for Economic Cooperation and Development report Monday said Britain's chances of having growth and low inflation are the best for 30 years but that interest rates will have to rise in 1997 to keep price pressures at bay.
U.K. chancellor Kenneth Clarke said Sunday he is willing to change rates to hit the government's inflation targets.

Currencies moved little when November U.S. industrial output and capacity use data. Capacity use rose to 83.3 percent against forecasts for an 83.0-percent rate. Industrial output rose 0.9 percent versus forecasts for up 0.6 percent.
December currency futures expired quietly at midmorning.

March yen eased $0.000010 to $0.008883, marks rose $0.0028 to $0.6500, Swiss francs firmed $0.0003 to $0.7625, Sterling jumped $0.0094 to $1.6620, Canadian dollar lost $0.0029 to $0.7355, Australian dollar added $0.0022 to $0.7932, and Mexican peso eased $0.000050 to $0.120250.
